_about: Issue taxonomy for construction RFIs. Learned from a corpus of real contractor RFIs (attachments, logs and consultant replies) and written in project-neutral terms so it applies to any project. Edit freely: tools/analyze_rfi_log.py re-measures how often each class occurs in any project's RFI log, and nodes/rfi_knowledge.py loads this file at run time.

issue_classes.title: Value conflict between documents
issue_classes.definition: The same item is given a different value in two documents (drawing vs BOQ vs specification vs schedule): rating, capacity, size, diameter, height, thickness, type, configuration, material, finish, quantity or count.
cues: equipment rating or capacity differs between a schematic/single-line diagram and the BOQ
dimension, height or diameter differs between a detail drawing and the BOQ description
product type, configuration or finish differs between the specification and the BOQ (e.g. single vs double glazing, galvanised vs painted)
cable, pipe or member size differs between a schedule and an updated drawing
device or equipment counts differ between a riser diagram and the BOQ
fire rating, density, wire size, capacity or equipment count stated one way in the BOQ and another in the drawings or specification
issue_classes.question_form: Please advise which value shall be followed: <doc 1 ref> states <value 1>, <doc 2 ref> states <value 2>.

issue_classes.title: Inconsistency within one document set
issue_classes.definition: Two sheets, views or sections of the SAME package disagree: plan vs section vs schedule, one single-line diagram vs another, floor plan vs riser diagram, general note vs specific detail, panel schedule vs SLD.
cues: the same load or panel is shown fed from two different sources on two diagrams
an equipment rating differs between two schematics of the same system
a member has two different levels, sizes or depths in plan and section
device quantities on floor plans do not match the riser/schematic diagram
a general note contradicts a specific callout or a typical detail
an element's size or type in plan differs from its schedule (column, footing, beam, door, wall schedules)
a dimension written as text differs from the size actually drawn
a detail or section does not match the plan it is referenced from
the centre of a footing does not coincide with the centre of the column it supports
issue_classes.question_form: Please confirm which arrangement shall be considered for construction: <sheet 1> shows <x>, <sheet 2> shows <y>.

issue_classes.title: Mismatch between discipline packages
issue_classes.definition: Architectural, structural, mechanical and electrical packages describe the same element or space differently, or one discipline shows an element the other does not support.
cues: beam depth or slab edge differs between structural and architectural drawings
an architectural wall or element has no structural support beneath it
a shaft or opening on the architectural plan is smaller than the duct or equipment that must pass through it
equipment shown in the mechanical design has no power feed or control panel in the electrical design
fixture or device type differs between architectural ceiling plans and electrical layouts
an element appears in one discipline's drawings with no information in the others
blockwork above or below is not aligned with the beam, core or wall it meets
a slab edge, opening or shaft is positioned or sized differently in architectural and structural drawings
an opening or shaft required by MEP drawings is missing from the structural drawings
architectural finished levels differ from structural slab levels for the same floor
grid axes of a building package do not match the master-plan package
ceiling plans and MEP layouts show different numbers or positions of fixtures, grilles or devices
issue_classes.question_form: Please review the mismatch between the <discipline 1> and <discipline 2> drawings at <location> and advise the required coordination.

issue_classes.title: Physical clash / interference
issue_classes.definition: Two elements occupy the same space or one blocks another once drawn to their real positions and levels: foundations overlapping, a pipe passing through a beam or tank, a cable route through a foundation, a ceiling below drop beams leaving no plenum, equipment blocking access or circulation.
cues: adjacent footings or a footing and a strip foundation overlap in plan
a buried service route runs through a foundation, fence base or manhole
drainage points sit directly above water tanks so pipes must pass through them
a services pipe level clashes with ground beams or a foundation
ceiling level intersects drop beams leaving insufficient plenum for MEP services
a new room or equipment location obstructs a driveway, door or access route
equipment plus its required clearance extends into windows, doors or another element
a pile, footing or tree pit intersects another foundation, utility or ramp
a duct or pipe passes through a beam, or a riser pipe obstructs a door
issue_classes.question_form: Please advise the required modification to resolve the clash between <element 1> and <element 2> at <location>.

issue_classes.title: Level / grading / coordinate conflict
issue_classes.definition: Levels, grades, inverts or coordinates of the same point or interface do not agree between packages, or the level difference they create is not catered for by the details.
cues: finished floor level vs adjacent external grade or sidewalk level differs between packages
retained soil height or level difference exceeds the limit assumed by the typical detail
entrance or threshold level does not match landscape/grading levels
invert levels of connecting pipes and manholes do not work
the same setting-out point has different coordinates in two packages
top-of-wall level vs landscape level is contradictory
issue_classes.question_form: Please confirm the governing level at <location>: <doc 1> gives <level 1>, <doc 2> gives <level 2>.

issue_classes.title: Missing information needed to build
issue_classes.definition: Information needed for shop drawings, procurement or construction is absent: a level, thickness, dimension, coordinate or orientation; a detail for a non-typical condition; a schedule; system data; a legend entry; a feed or route; or a whole drawing set for a scope item.
cues: a level, slab thickness, dimension or coordinate is not given for an element that must be built
a non-typical condition (taller wall, special junction) has no detail
door, window, finishes, signage or load schedules are not provided
equipment technical data is missing (duty, static pressure, voltage/phase/frequency, capacity)
a symbol, tag or fixture code used on plans has no description in the legend or schedule
a feeder, cable route or connection is not shown for equipment that needs one
a discipline package (e.g. MEP for a building, structure for a kiosk) is missing
an element on plan has no type, tag or mark, or its mark is absent from the schedule
slab, stair or drop-panel thickness, reinforcement or level is not given
finishes, door/hardware schedules, signage or elevation drawings are missing for an area
issue_classes.question_form: Kindly provide <the missing information> for <element/location> to enable shop drawings and execution.

issue_classes.title: Scope gap between drawings/specification and BOQ
issue_classes.definition: An item is shown or specified but has no BOQ item (or a BOQ item has no design), or a BOQ item lacks its quantity or description. Usually carries a variation-order implication.
cues: an item appears on the drawings but is not included in the BOQ
the specification requires a system or component that is not priced
a BOQ item has no corresponding design, location or detail
a BOQ line has no quantity or no description
an instruction adds an element that was not in the tender basis
an item drawn or specified is listed in the BOQ only as optional, rate-only or free-issue
a drawn element type (e.g. a footing or wall type) has no matching BOQ item
issue_classes.question_form: Please confirm whether <item> is within the contractor's scope; if required, it will be treated as a variation.
keywords: neither included in the project boq
while it has not been included

issue_classes.title: Design change between revisions or stages
issue_classes.definition: A later revision, stage (tender -> IFC) or instruction changes ratings, components, locations or scope relative to the earlier basis, or deletes/relocates something leaving related items undefined.
cues: ratings or component counts increased between revision 00 and revision 01
the IFC drawing adds equipment or panels absent from the tender drawings the BOQ was priced on
a site instruction relocates or adds an element that conflicts with the IFC set
a room is deleted or re-purposed and its finishes, services or levels are left undefined
a later package contradicts an earlier clarification
a new instruction or package changes elements that were already built or approved
two revisions of the same package disagree
issue_classes.question_form: Please confirm the revised requirement and note that the change relative to <earlier basis> affects cost/programme.

issue_classes.title: Interface, tie-in or scope boundary
issue_classes.definition: The connection between this package and another (another building, plot, contractor, utility or package) is undefined: tie-in location, level or coordinates, feeding source, sleeves, spare lengths, or where the contractor's scope stops.
cues: tie-in location, level or coordinates for a service to a plot or building outside the package
source of supply for a panel, barrier or system is not identified
interface between external network and building connection is not detailed
number, size and level of sleeves for incoming services is not defined
the scope limit at a house/building connection is unclear
issue_classes.question_form: Please provide the location, level and arrangement of the <service> tie-in at <interface>, and confirm the scope boundary.

issue_classes.title: Technical adequacy, code compliance or constructability
issue_classes.definition: The design as drawn does not work technically or cannot be built as shown: a calculation limit is exceeded, a code requirement is not met, or the available space/depth/mounting condition does not suit the specified item.
cues: voltage drop, cable length or loop/device capacity exceeds the applicable limit
hazard or occupancy classification is inconsistent with the governing code
available depth is insufficient for a pipe, its fittings and the required slope
a specified vent, valve or component size is below the code minimum
normal and emergency circuits share a containment that should be segregated
a component type does not suit its mounting condition (e.g. recessed fitting on a wall with no void)
a room is too small for the equipment and its required clearances
a specified product is larger than the wall, room or void meant to hold it (cabinet deeper than the wall, fitting longer than the room)
a recessed fitting is specified where there is no false ceiling
a door's clear opening is below the accessibility minimum
the false-ceiling height leaves too little space for the coordinated MEP services
issue_classes.question_form: Please review the attached check and confirm the proposed solution, or advise.

issue_classes.title: Ambiguous or incomplete specification
issue_classes.definition: A specification or BOQ is internally ambiguous or incomplete: a general clause contradicts an item description, a specification section exists for one package but not another, the measurement basis is unclear, or a typical detail's applicability is unclear.
cues: a general description in the BOQ contradicts specific items of the same BOQ
a system is specified only in another package's specification
the basis of a stated dimension is unclear (internal vs external diameter)
it is unclear on which face or zone a typical detail applies
an item code does not match its written description
issue_classes.question_form: Please clarify <the ambiguous requirement> so that it can be applied consistently.

issue_classes.title: Inconsistency between repeated / typical units
issue_classes.definition: Buildings, floors, rooms or zones declared to be of the same type (typical floors, sister buildings, repeated rooms) are designed differently in some respect - door widths, hardware, fire protection system, fixtures, equipment or finishes - with no stated reason.
cues: two buildings of the same type have different door widths, hardware sets or fixture counts
a fire protection system differs between identical rooms in different buildings
one typical floor shows an item (access door, valve, opening) that the other typical floors lack
the same room type has different finishes or ceiling heights between buildings
issue_classes.question_form: Please confirm whether <unit 1> shall follow <unit 2>, as both are of the same type.

issue_classes.title: Approved submittal / shop drawing vs design
issue_classes.definition: An approved material submittal, shop drawing, inspection comment or earlier RFI reply contradicts the IFC drawings, the BOQ or another approval - e.g. the approved product type differs from the one drawn, or an inspection rejects what an approved shop drawing shows.
cues: the approved material submittal specifies a type (recessed, surface, capacity) different from the IFC drawings
an inspection or review comment contradicts an approved shop drawing
a consultant comment on a shop drawing requires something absent from the IFC and BOQ
two RFI replies or two approvals for the same element disagree
issue_classes.question_form: Please advise whether the approved <submittal> or the <IFC/BOQ> shall govern.

issue_classes.title: Specified product unavailable / substitution
issue_classes.definition: A specified product, size, capacity or vendor is not available on the market, so an alternative is proposed. Not detectable by comparing documents; recorded so drafting and classification recognise it.
issue_classes.question_form: Please confirm acceptance of the proposed alternative <product>, as the specified <product> is not available.

issue_classes.title: Contractor proposal for approval
issue_classes.definition: The contractor submits an alternative, a design check result or a method (shoring, construction joints, pipe rating, layout adjustment) for the consultant's approval. Raised by the contractor's own initiative, not by comparing documents; recorded so drafting can phrase proposals.
issue_classes.question_form: Kindly review and approve the attached proposal, otherwise please advise.

issue_classes.title: Design vs existing site conditions
issue_classes.definition: The design does not fit what exists on site: as-built levels, existing foundations or utilities, relocated manholes, natural ground levels. Detectable only when an as-built, survey or site record is one of the compared documents.
cues: executed or as-built levels differ from the design levels
existing utilities or foundations occupy the designed location
natural ground level differs significantly from the design grade
work executed by a previous contractor does not match the design now issued
issue_classes.question_form: Please provide the as-built information / instruction needed to coordinate <element> with the existing condition.

not_discrepancies: Values at DIFFERENT physical locations are expected to differ: two sections, sheets, axes, buildings or panels showing different levels or sizes is not a conflict.
A position on the sheet (top-left, bottom-right, sheet centre) is NOT a physical location. Never pair or compare items just because they sit in the same part of two different sheets.

Section, panel, bay or element identifiers (e.g. 'SEC 3-3', a bay mark between two posts, a panel or manhole number) are location labels, not grid lines; two different identifiers are two different places, not a 'grid conflict'.
The same requirement written with different notation, units or rounding (mm vs m, 'nr' vs 'no.', bar notation styles) is a representation difference, not a discrepancy.
One document carrying more detail than another is not a discrepancy unless the extra detail changes cost, programme, quality or responsibility.
Statements that something is NOT visible in a crop or tile are not information about the project and are never compared.
Revision numbers, dates and title-block differences between two different drawings are not discrepancies unless one document refers to a superseded revision of the other.
A value that could not be read is an item for human review (ambiguity, minor) - never a contradiction.
Buildings, floors or zones of DIFFERENT types legitimately differ; only units declared to be of the same type (typical floors, sister buildings) are expected to match.
A dimension, level or size given on one side only, with nothing to compare against, is not a conflict - at most it is missing information on the other side.

rfi_style.opening: Start from the documents: 'With reference to <drawing/BOQ/specification/instruction reference>, it is noted that:'
rfi_style.grouping: Related points on the same system, element or area go into ONE RFI as numbered points (observed up to 11 points per RFI). Unrelated subjects get separate RFIs.
rfi_style.point_form: Each point is SHORT: one sentence naming the element and the problem, then one line per source quoting what it says with its reference (e.g. 'Architectural A-502: beam 250x500' / 'Structural S-208: beam 200x500'), then the question. No restating, no background inside the point.

closing_by_request_type.which_governs: Please advise which shall be followed.
closing_by_request_type.provide_information: Kindly provide the required information to enable us to proceed.
closing_by_request_type.confirm_scope: Please confirm whether this item is within our scope of work.
closing_by_request_type.resolve_clash: Please advise the required modification to resolve this conflict.
closing_by_request_type.confirm_proposal: Kindly review and confirm the proposed solution, otherwise please advise.

rfi_style.commercial_note: When the clarification may add work beyond the BOQ / tender basis, state neutrally that any additional scope will be treated as a variation order.
rfi_style.attachments: Refer to the evidence as attachments ('see attach. 1') so the reader can find each marked-up source.
subject_patterns: Conflict between architectural and structural drawings - <element> at <location>
example_points: Door fire rating: the drawings give 90 min, the BOQ gives 45 min. Please advise which shall be followed.
Column at axis X/Y: plan shows 900x900, the column schedule shows 600x1200. Please advise which shall be followed.
Roof beam: architectural detail shows 250x500, structural plan shows 200x500; at 200 mm it clashes with the 250 mm wall. Please advise.
Basement rooms: wall types and door types are not indicated. Kindly provide them.

corpus_observations._note: Measured from two learning corpora (an infrastructure/mixed-use project and a multi-building business district) by tools/analyze_rfi_log.py; per-project output in knowledge/corpus_stats/. Used for weighting and documentation only - never as project-specific rules.
